# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a red light, display 0, and an embossed warning: “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” The three wires are 1 red, 2 green, and 3 yellow. I am establishing the required gesture vocabulary: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✋ means HOLD, and 👌 means DONE. I am sending the visual bomb information to both teammates by speech and the gesture meanings to Mute by sight and speech.

```text
speak(text="I see display 0, red light, embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Gesture code: thumbs up means YES, thumbs down means NO, raised palm means HOLD, OK sign means DONE.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s thumbs-up confirms YES, so the gesture code was received. No new bomb information has appeared, and the warning still forbids cutting any wire. I will wait for the manual’s instructions and Blind’s report of what can be operated.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The repeated thumbs-up confirms the code, but it does not yet identify the manual’s verdict or an operation. The warning still explicitly forbids cutting wires. I am asking Mute to report the manual’s instruction using the established gesture vocabulary; until that arrives, Blind should hold.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please report the manual verdict using the established gestures: YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE. Blind, HOLD until the verdict is relayed.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s thumbs-up reports a YES verdict from the manual. Blind’s raised hand is not part of our agreed code, so I cannot safely interpret it as HOLD. I am relaying the manual verdict to Blind by speech, as required, while giving no wire-cutting instruction because the bomb explicitly says not to cut any wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict: YES. Do not cut any wire. The raised-hand signal is not part of our agreed code; HOLD until a valid instruction is available.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The manual’s YES remains the only confirmed verdict, while the bomb still forbids cutting any wire. Blind has not provided a signal in the agreed vocabulary, so no safe operation is identified. I will continue holding rather than invent an interpretation.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information has arrived. The bomb still shows no permitted wire action, and the earlier YES only confirmed a response, not the specific operation. I need Mute to identify whether the manual instructs Blind to do nothing; I will keep Blind on HOLD while asking that question.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual instruct Blind to do nothing? Reply with YES or NO using the established gesture code.")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The manual's specific operation is not yet identified; do not cut any wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s NO means the manual does not instruct Blind to do nothing, so some active operation is required. Blind’s 🖐 is not our agreed HOLD symbol (✋), so I cannot treat it as a valid report. The warning rules out cutting any wire; I am narrowing the manual’s instruction by asking whether it specifies wire 1, while telling Blind to remain still.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual specifically instruct cutting wire 1? Reply YES or NO with the established gesture code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual requires an active operation, but the bomb forbids cutting wires. HOLD; do not cut any wire.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s YES confirms that the manual specifically refers to wire 1, but this conflicts directly with the visible embossed warning not to cut any wire. I must not turn that partial confirmation into a cutting command. Blind’s 🖐 is not the agreed HOLD symbol, so I cannot use it as a reliable status report. I am asking Mute for the manual’s exact action and keeping Blind still.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The manual's wire 1 reference conflicts with the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning. What exact action does the manual require? Do not answer only YES or NO; report the action using ordinary words if needed.")
speak(to="blind", text="There is a conflict: the manual refers to wire 1, but the bomb says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not cut or alter anything; HOLD.")
```
